result:
Fixed in `anthrouter/pace.py`. September 2026 now gives 22 workdays for UTC.

**Cause:** `period_workday_dates` treated `period_end` as inclusive. But `period_end` is the first instant of the next month, so Oct 1 (a Thursday) was counted as a September workday.

**Fix:** `end_local` is now the local date of `period_end - 1µs`. This also fixes timezones east of UTC the same way. Timezones west of UTC are unaffected, since their local end date was already the last day of the month.

I ran `workday_elapsed_pct` for 2026-09-10 in UTC and it returned `(31.8…, 22)`. I did not run the test suite, because `pytest` isn't installed in this environment. Existing tests that hard-code workday counts for other months or timezones may need a look.
